decisions.reason: The original unconditional extension claim fails for the mixed chart L0=A0(v+w)+qA0v: E_Z=Z(v+w) but M=A v+A w has rank two. Added balancedness to both extension and basis assertions, matching parts (1) and (2) of the two-chart lemma. The residue-map definition and inverse globalization convention are unchanged.

F2 misnamed the algebra multiplication: products mix degrees by (AB)_nu=sum_{beta+gamma=nu} A_beta B_gamma, as the completion definition states. Corrected F2. The dual-basis matrix calculation and finite-support weight-shift proof never multiply completed families, so their conclusions remain valid; this is a nonfatal dependency restatement defect.

The old step 6.1 inferred a multiplication congruence absent from F1's Statement. Replaced it with the primitive projection P_i=1-tilde f_i tilde e_i, the integral divided-power decomposition, and an explicit quotient-basis coefficient argument. In the exact n-position quotient the coefficients are Laurent polynomials regular at zero and bar fixed, hence integers; their residues force 1 at tilde f_i^n b and 0 elsewhere. This proves the original assertion (v) without weakening it. Read Kashiwara91 sections 7.2–7.5, printed pp.512–516, to check the induction and quotient-chart hypotheses; the new coefficient argument is supplied locally.

F3 falsely made the entire crystal-to-basis-or-zero map bijective: in rank one at lambda=0 every positive divided-power class maps to zero. Corrected F3 to state a bijection only on the surviving domain, exactly as F1 and the projection supplier require. The proof already uses the survivor bijection and an adapted common global basis for the integral kernel, so the kernel and based-quotient statements remain sound.

L2 omitted the required weight decomposition and misidentified a residue basis as crystal-lattice data. Restated all three lattice axioms and separated the crystal-basis datum; made the scaled trivial lattice's zero-weight decomposition explicit in step 3.1. Direct coordinate intersections still give rank-one failure of surjectivity for the mixed chart and kernel Z v+Z qv for the scaled trivial chart, with the two stated distinct bar-fixed lifts.

Step 1.2 placed the toral weight on the wrong factor. With n'=E-word input of second weight mu, its actual t-term scalar is q_i^{-t(mu(h_i)+r-t)}. Replaced the prose by the exact semilinear induction recursion. This factor-location error is nonfatal for the claimed integrality: the true scalar is still a Laurent unit and every t>=1 term still lowers second height. Also corrected the coproduct citations, which the named reordering interfaces did not supply, by adding the actual Hopf supplier and deriving the divided formulas locally in step 1.1. Consulted Bao–Wang's full seven-page argument and Lusztig sections 6.3.3–6.3.6, 24.1.1–24.1.6, 27.1.2–27.1.8, checking the flipped order and the finite-type and supported-globalization qualifications.

The lowering-string formula in L1 needed n>=1 for tilde e. Added that restriction, n>=0 for tilde f, and the separate tilde e(1)=0 endpoint. The rank-one norm/product identities, A2 primitive-word lifts, Gram determinant 1-q^2 and its displayed inverse duals remain correct at all admissible indices, including the empty product at n=0. The proof does not require a negative divided power.

Extending an A=Z[q,q^{-1}] lattice by A0-span gives the entire field module, since it contains every negative q-power; it cannot give the crystal chart. Replaced this false inference in the Example and step 1.2 by scalar extension of C0=sum Z[q]w_n and C0^vee=sum Z[q]w_n^up. Their A0-spans agree because d_{m,n} and its inverse are units congruent to 1. The inverse-Gram lattice, adjoint bar and nonzero A/(1+q^2) quotient remain unchanged. Also restricted the norm recurrence to 1<=n<=m to exclude its undefined zero-index denominator.

The Example called E_Z-to-residues globalization, although the definition reserves that name for the inverse. Renamed that arrow canonical reduction and stated the inverse sends [v],[w] to v,w in step 1.1. Both arrows are isomorphisms here, so the balancedness, finite quasi-R matrix, correction c=q, corrected tensor basis and mixed-chart failure were already valid; this is a nonfatal direction/naming defect.
